standard_prerequisites.name: The regular-model situation, torsion in Picard groups and the thickenings of the special fibre
standard_prerequisites.statement: The situation fixes a discrete valuation ring with residue field, a smooth projective curve over its fraction field, a regular proper model and the components of the special fibre; the reduction of the fibre sits inside it as a closed subscheme whose successive thickenings are cut out by powers of the uniformizer, and the whole model is recovered as the formal completion along the reduction. For a class in the Picard group that is annihilated by an integer prime to the residue characteristic, triviality on the reduction implies triviality on every thickening and then on the completion, and the completion determines the scheme in the relevant sense. The author's own lemmas of the chapter and the quoted results of the Coherent, More on Algebra and More on Morphisms chapters are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is the comparison that lets the chapter move torsion information between the model and the reduction of its special fibre, and it is what makes the study of the Picard group of a model effective.

core_obligations: Set up the thickenings: the base change of the model along the successive quotients of the discrete valuation ring is the corresponding thickening of the reduction, each of them finite over the residue field and hence with controlled cohomology of coherent sheaves (source lines 6005-6015).

Propagate triviality from the reduction to every thickening: an invertible sheaf that is trivial on the reduction and whose class is annihilated by an integer prime to the residue characteristic is trivial on each thickening, which the proof obtains by comparing the Picard groups of the thickenings through the quoted results on torsion under a thickening (source lines 6015-6030).

Pass to the completion: a coherent sheaf supported on the special fibre is annihilated by a power of the uniformizer, so the theorem on formal functions applies to the model along its special fibre and the triviality on all thickenings implies triviality on the completion (source lines 6030-6038).

Return to the model: the completion determines the original invertible sheaf, which the proof supplies through the comparison of completions, so the class is trivial on the model itself, that is, the map of the statement is injective (source lines 6038-6042).

proof_roadmap.step: Identify the thickenings of the reduction with the base changes of the model.
Propagate triviality from the reduction to all thickenings using torsion under a thickening.
Apply the theorem on formal functions to pass to the completion.
Compare completions to conclude triviality on the model.
